articles.title: Is it a ‘honeypot’ or a ‘honeytrap’?
articles.summary: As news broke that the Nvidia CEO might have fallen victim to an age-old spying tactic, people were divided on what to call it.
articles.body: Over the weekend, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged that he had an affair with a woman who US intelligence officials had separately suspected was a spy for the Chinese government, setting off an ongoing corporate crisis at the chip-making behemoth that culminated in Huang’s resignation on Thursday. You catch more trade secrets with honey than with vinegar, to paraphrase an old idiom. But when you do it, are you using a “honeypot”? Or is it a “honeytrap”? As journalists and other observers processed the news that one of the world’s most powerful men might have fallen victim to an age-old spying tactic, they were divided on what to call it. References to honeypots and honeytraps both abounded — deployed as nouns or as verbs, and with or without a space between “honey” and the rest of the compound. The “-trap” enthusiasts included CNN — “Was Nvidia’s CEO honey-trapped?” we asked in a video — and The Spectator, which proclaimed “Long live honeytraps!” Elsewhere, “honeypot” was the word that stuck. “Nvidia Gets a Chinese Honeypot Lesson,” read the headline of a Wall Street Journal op-ed. Reuters opted for the two-word form, with the headline “Nvidia’s close-knit board comes under pressure with ‘honey pot’ test.” The American Prospect wrote of “The Honeypot That Might End the AI Boom,” going on to say in the article that the Nvidia boss “got honeypotted by a dadgummed Chinese spy.” Was there a distinction between the “honeypot” and the “honeytrap”? In some instances, people used “honeypot” to refer to the woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset, and “honeytrap” for the alleged operation itself. But plenty of others used both words interchangeably. “‘Honeypots’ or ‘honey traps’—positioning an alluring operative to seduce or develop a relationship with a key target—are one of intelligence’s most infamous and well-established strategies,” went one explanation in Wired. Wordsmiths insisted that conflating the two terms was wrong. “The normalization of ‘honeypot’ over honeytrap is the real scandal here,” Gady Epstein, a longform editor at The Economist, wrote on Bluesky. Merriam-Webster signaled where it stood on the issue by posting its entry for “honey trap,” defined as “a scheme in criminal activity or in espionage that involves using the possibility of a romantic or sexual relationship to lure someone into a compromising position often for the purpose of blackmailing them.” The practice of using seduction to obtain an advantage over an enemy goes back thousands of years. In the Bible, Samson falls in love with Delilah, who the Philistines bribed with silver to ascertain the source of Samson’s superhuman strength. But the use of the “honey-” words for it is much more recent. “Honeytrap,” in the sense of the espionage operation, sounds like timeworn cloak-and-dagger professional jargon, but it was made up by the author John le Carré, in his 1974 novel “Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy.” In 1976, le Carré said in a BBC interview that a “honeytrap” is “where you put a girl in a chap’s way; it’s a sexual enticement operation.” “John Le Carré” was a pseudonym used by the former British intelligence officer David Cromwell, because the government prohibited agents from publishing under their own names. He was likewise required to avoid revealing real tradecraft — and so, he told the BBC interviewer, he had invented a whole fictional vocabulary for the profession, using words like “honeytrap,’ “lamplighters,” and “scalphunters” that actual intelligence officers had never heard of. The premise of the “honeytrap” proved irresistible for spy novelists and tabloid journalists, who often based their depictions on dubious accounts from intelligence agents, journalist Henry Schlesinger wrote in a 2022 article. Women enlisted to carry out such schemes were frequently portrayed in pop culture as femme fatales, even as real life operations were less salacious, he wrote. But the trope stuck, and over the years, the word “honeytrap” did, too. What, then, of the “honeypot”? The Oxford English Dictionary traces it back to around 1475, when it appeared in the English-Latin dictionary “Catholicon Anglicum” to describe a vessel for holding the sticky nectar concentrate produced by bees. Over time, “honeypot” developed a number of other meanings: In the early 17th century, it was used to refer to an alluring or tempting person, whether the tempter had ulterior motives or not. “A Whore entring into a Prison is a Hony-pot about which all the flyes come buzzing, as Crowes to a Carrion,” English writer Geffray Mynshul wrote in his satirical “Essayes and Characters of a Prison and Prisoners.” In the latter half of the 17th century, the word was also invoked as a euphemism for female genitals. “Honeypot” would additionally come to describe a player in a Scottish children’s game, a type of ant and a makeshift toilet. As “honeytrap” took hold as a term for an intelligence operation involving romance or sex, “honeypot” emerged in the ’90s as a term for a different but conceptually similar kind of temptation: a decoy website or network set up to as a false target to catch cybercriminals. Somewhere along the way, people apparently started to use the two words interchangeably to refer to the seduction scheme. This has been happening for at least 15 years, based on a 2011 entry for “honeypot” in Urban Dictionary, which defined it as “a sting operation that involves one going undercover to seduce an (usually high profile) individual into a compromising position for future extortion purposes.” Why the two words were conflated is less clear. Sreemoy Talukdar, an editor for the Indian news website Firstpost, chalked it up to a frustrating Yankeeism. “Why do Americans have to invent a new word for everything?” he wrote on X. “Pavement is sidewalk. Spectacles are eyeglasses. And now we have ‘honeypot’ for honeytrap.” But does it really matter whether you call it a “honeypot” or a “honeytrap”? The Museum of English Rural Life, an authority on another kind of honeypot, made light of the distinction while also using it. After joining the excitement of the Jensen Huang news cycle by sharing an image of a honey-storing vessel from its collection on its Bluesky account, the museum responded to persnickety critics who accused it of using the incorrect term. “To all the people arguing in our mentions that it’s honeytrap not honeypot: congratulations, you have been caught in The Museum of English Rural Life’s honeypot honeytrap.”

articles.title: AI, talent gaps and labour reforms: Forces redefining India's employment landscape
articles.summary: By Balasubramaniam A India's employment landscape is undergoing a fundamental shift.
articles.body: By Balasubramaniam AIndia's employment landscape is undergoing a fundamental shift. The conversation is no longer limited to how many jobs the economy can create. It is increasingly about the nature of these jobs, the skills they demand, the security they offer and how prepared India's workforce is to participate in this changing world of work.Three forces are driving this transition: the rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), an expanding gap between the skills employers need and those available in the workforce, and the implementation of new labour codes. Together, they are changing not just how organisations hire, but also how people work, earn and build their careers.The latest TeamLease Employment Outlook Report for HY2 FY 2026-27 offers some interesting insights into this transition. Based on a survey of 1,239 businesses across 23 industries and 20 cities, the report projects a Net Employment Change of 5.4%, up from 4.7% in HY1 FY 2026-27. While 60% of employers plan to expand their workforce, compared with 58% in the previous half-year, the nature of this expansion is becoming increasingly selective.For employees, this means that opportunities are growing, but the expectations attached to them are changing.AI is expanding the possibilities of workArtificial Intelligence is opening up new possibilities across India's employment landscape. From improving operational efficiency and enabling better decision-making to changing how routine tasks are performed, AI is influencing how people contribute to business outcomes. As organisations integrate AI into their workflows, employees are increasingly expected to work alongside these tools, adapt to changing processes and develop capabilities that complement automation.The Employment Outlook Report highlights that 85% of employers report some workforce use of AI or Generative AI tools. However, only 13% report adoption across more than half their workforce, while 54% restrict usage to a quarter of employees or fewer. The most common adoption level is between 11% and 25% of the workforce, indicating that AI deployment remains largely concentrated within specific functions rather than being embedded across entire organisations.For employees, this points to a transition that is still taking shape. AI is increasingly being layered onto existing roles rather than fundamentally changing every job. Applications such as routing and scheduling in logistics, assisted diagnostics in service networks and query handling in customer operations illustrate how technology can support everyday responsibilities.The opportunity lies in ensuring that employees are equipped to work effectively with these tools. As AI adoption deepens, organisations will need to focus not just on technology deployment but also on helping their workforce understand, adopt and use these capabilities responsibly.The real employment challenge is the skills gapOne of the biggest challenges facing India's labour market is the growing disconnect between available talent and the capabilities employers require.The report identifies digital literacy as the most sought-after workforce competency, with 59% of employers identifying it as a priority. Customer experience management follows at 51%, while communication skills stand at 48%. Teamwork and collaboration and adaptability both feature at 44%.What is particularly interesting is that these are not skills limited to technology professionals. Digital literacy is increasingly becoming a baseline requirement across blue-collar and white-collar roles alike. A warehouse worker may need to navigate digital inventory systems, while a retail employee must increasingly work with digital payment, reporting and customer engagement platforms.This tells us something important about the future of employability. Being skilled will no longer mean simply being proficient in one particular trade or function. It will mean having the ability to combine domain knowledge with digital fluency, communication and adaptability.However, the challenge extends beyond identifying the skills required. The report finds that 72% of employers planning workforce expansion anticipate significant or moderate difficulty in achieving their hiring numbers. The challenge is particularly visible in IT, where 39% of employers report hiring difficulty, followed by Sales and Marketing at 38%, Engineering at 32% and blue-collar roles at 31%. Among employers anticipating hiring difficulty, IT roles are the most commonly cited at 39%, followed by Sales and Marketing at 38%, Engineering at 32% and blue-collar roles at 31%.This highlights an important disconnect: while employment opportunities are growing, finding people with the right capabilities remains a significant challenge.The opportunity for India lies in its demographic scale. However, a large workforce alone does not guarantee a competitive advantage. We need to invest in continuous skilling, accessible vocational education, apprenticeships and industry-aligned training.Equally important is making reskilling accessible to people already in employment. A worker should not have to wait until their role becomes redundant to acquire new skills. Employers, educational institutions and skilling ecosystems must create pathways that allow people to transition into emerging opportunities without disrupting their livelihoods.The emphasis must shift from training people for their first job to preparing them for multiple career transitions over their working lives.Labour reforms must translate into better outcomes for workersThe third force shaping India's employment landscape is labour reform. The four new Labour Codes, which came into effect on 21 November 2025, consolidate 29 central labour laws and represent an important step towards simplifying India's employment framework, strengthening formalisation and bringing greater consistency to employment practices.However, the impact of these reforms will ultimately be measured by how they change the experience of workers.The TeamLease report indicates that 39% of employers identify increased compliance and payroll administration effort as the leading impact of the Labour Codes. This is followed by higher employer statutory contribution costs, reported by 35% of employers. Further, 28% anticipate moderation in salary increments due to higher employment costs, while an equal proportion foresee a possible reduction in employee take-home pay due to salary restructuring.These changes have direct implications for employees. A restructuring of salary components can influence the relationship between take-home pay and long-term social security contributions. Where existing salary structures have a lower basic pay component and higher allowances, aligning compensation with the statutory wage definition may increase the base for contributions.This is where transparency becomes critical. Employers must communicate compensation changes clearly, helping employees understand not just what their salary structure looks like, but also what it means for their monthly earnings and financial security over time.The reforms also bring an opportunity to strengthen formal employment practices, improve compliance and extend greater protection to workers. For India's large workforce, including those in contractual and emerging employment arrangements, the focus must be on making formalisation meaningful.The growth of gig and platform-based work makes this particularly relevant. With more people participating in flexible and technology-enabled employment models, the conversation around social security, worker protection and access to benefits must evolve alongside the nature of work itself.The future of work must be built around peopleIndia's employment outlook is encouraging. The report shows that hiring momentum is strongest in digital-first and consumer-facing sectors, with e-commerce and technology start-ups projecting strengthening across sectors, with e-commerce and technology start-ups recording a Net Employment Change of 12.6%, Travel and Hospitality 12.3%, and Retail 10.3%. Automotive and EV and EV Infrastructure are also witnessing strong hiring momentum, with Net Employment Changes of 10.1% and 9.7%, respectively.But the larger opportunity is not simply to create more jobs. It is to create an employment ecosystem where people can access opportunities, develop relevant skills, earn fairly and build sustainable careers.This requires a collective effort. Employers must invest in their workforce beyond immediate hiring requirements. Governments must ensure that policy reforms translate into meaningful worker protection. Educational institutions must align learning with the changing demands of industry. And employees must be encouraged and supported to embrace lifelong learning.We must also ensure that the benefits of this transition are not concentrated in a few sectors or metropolitan centres. Emerging industrial hubs, Tier-2 cities and digitally connected smaller markets can play a significant role in distributing employment opportunities more widely.Ultimately, AI will change how we work, skill gaps will determine who can participate in emerging opportunities, and labour reforms will influence the quality and security of employment. These forces are interconnected, and addressing them in isolation will not be enough.India stands at an important moment in its workforce evolution. Our demographic advantage will deliver its full potential only when people have the skills, opportunities and protections needed to succeed. The future of employment should not just be about building a more productive workforce. It should be about building a more empowered one.(The author is Senior Vice President, TeamLease Services)Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Jensen Huang's scandal: Chinese spy, Kimberly Powell and Nvidia's crisis explained in 10 points
articles.summary: Little more than a week ago, Jensen Huang was among the most influential people in the world.
articles.body: Little more than a week ago, Jensen Huang was among the most influential people in the world. One of the richest men on the planet, the chief executive of Nvidia was a regular fixture at high-profile technology gatherings, enjoyed access to US President Donald Trump and had even attended a state dinner at the White House. As the man at the helm of the world's most valuable chipmaker, Huang was arguably one of the most consequential figures in the artificial intelligence revolution.Today, his position looks considerably more precarious. The 63-year-old billionaire, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and transformed it into a roughly $4 trillion technology giant, is facing mounting scrutiny over allegations of two extramarital relationships, one involving a Chinese businesswoman identified by US intelligence officials as a suspected Chinese spy and another involving a senior executive who reports directly to him.The latest revelation, reported by The New York Times, has intensified an already unfolding crisis. Five people who worked at Nvidia told the newspaper that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of healthcare. The report said the two were seen being affectionate at a hotel during Nvidia's annual developer conference in March. The newspaper said it had not independently seen the video that allegedly captured the interaction.The second relationshipThe latest development emerged in a report by The New York Times, which said Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare. Citing five people who worked at the company, the newspaper reported that the two were seen being affectionate at a hotel in San Jose, California, during Nvidia's annual GTC developer conference in March. Both Huang, 63, and Powell, 48, are married to other people. The report is particularly significant because Powell is a senior executive within Nvidia and, according to the newspaper's sources, reports to Huang. The development has raised fresh questions about executive conduct and the company's internal governance.Who is Kimberly PowellPowell is not an outsider or a relatively unknown figure at Nvidia. She joined the company in 2008 and has spent nearly two decades rising through its ranks. According to her LinkedIn profile, she was promoted to senior director of artificial intelligence business development in 2016 before becoming vice president of healthcare in late 2017. She oversees initiatives involving the application of Nvidia's chip technology to healthcare and higher education, particularly medical imaging. Powell also represents the company at international technology conferences. At the March GTC conference, she delivered a presentation on how artificial intelligence could help advance healthcare and biology, using cartoon depictions of Huang during her presentation.The alleged hotel encounter and the NDAAccording to the New York Times, the alleged relationship had been discussed within Nvidia for some time. Two people familiar with the incident told the newspaper that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel where Nvidia executives were holding meetings during the March conference. A bystander allegedly recorded the interaction on a mobile phone. Three people briefed on the incident said Huang's security personnel noticed the individual recording the encounter and subsequently isolated them. The security workers then allegedly asked the bystander to sign a non-disclosure agreement. The newspaper said it had not seen the video itself, and the claims have not been independently verified.What did Huang say when confrontedWhen contacted by The New York Times on Wednesday and asked directly about his relationship with Powell, Huang reportedly responded: "I don't think you should be talking to me directly." He then hung up. Nvidia declined to provide a statement, while Powell did not immediately respond to the newspaper's request for comment. The latest report follows Huang's earlier admission to Nvidia's board that he had been unfaithful to his wife. In that communication, he did not identify the woman involved. The company has not publicly confirmed the allegations concerning Powell. The absence of an official response has, however, added to the uncertainty surrounding the unfolding controversy.The Alice Huang connection: The alleged Chinese spyThe Powell revelation comes against the backdrop of a separate controversy involving Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le. An earlier New York Times investigation reported that US intelligence officials had identified her as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. She allegedly developed a close personal relationship with Huang and attempted to influence Nvidia's approach towards making its advanced AI chips more accessible to China. The two are not related. Huang subsequently acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, although he did not identify Alice. Beijing has strongly rejected the espionage allegations, calling them groundless accusations and a smear campaign against China. Alice Huang has not publicly responded to the claims.Megaspeed and the billion-dollar chip controversyAlice Huang's professional connections have brought another company into the controversy: Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International. She became associated with the company in 2023, serving as its managing director for approximately eight months. Megaspeed has faced US scrutiny over allegations that it helped divert advanced Nvidia processors to China, bypassing Washington's export restrictions. Its assets reportedly surged from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024, while revenue reached $294 million. Singapore police have been investigating the company since October 2025 over suspected breaches of domestic laws. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and says it takes US export-control obligations extremely seriously.Why Nvidia's chips have become a geopolitical flashpointThe controversy is about more than the personal relationships of a billionaire executive. Nvidia dominates the market for high-end graphics processing units (GPUs), the specialised chips used to train and operate advanced AI systems. Its products have become critical infrastructure for the global AI industry, with estimates placing its share of the high-end AI chip market above 80%. Washington has restricted exports of its most powerful processors to China since 2022, seeking to prevent Beijing from gaining access to technology that could strengthen its military and technological capabilities. Huang, meanwhile, has repeatedly advocated relaxing export restrictions, arguing that maintaining Nvidia's presence in China would help preserve American technological leadership.The US government, Congress and Trump's connectionThe allegations have also drawn Washington's attention. Republican leaders of three influential House committees have sought a closed-door briefing from Huang about his interactions with Alice Huang. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast has indicated that a congressional subpoena could follow if the Nvidia chief does not agree to appear personally. Meanwhile, reports have raised questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's handling of investigations involving Megaspeed. Axios reported that Lutnick had repeatedly reversed efforts to hold the company accountable amid concerns about escalating trade tensions with Beijing. The Commerce Department denied reports of a confrontation with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent over the matter. Trump, meanwhile, has publicly defended Huang, calling him an "honorable guy".Nvidia's board is now considering Huang's futureThe second relationship allegation appears to have changed the atmosphere inside Nvidia's boardroom. According to Reuters, the board had met to discuss Huang's future, marking a shift from its earlier expression of confidence in the chief executive and his leadership team. The Wall Street Journal also reported that Nvidia was preparing to fire Huang, triggering a sharp reaction in the markets. Huang has led the company for more than three decades and owns approximately 3.6% of its stock. He has more than 60 direct reports, with no obvious successor waiting in the wings. Analysts have identified CFO Colette Kress and senior engineer Ian Buck as possible candidates should the board decide to replace him.What happens to Nvidia and the global AI boom?The uncertainty surrounding Huang has extended well beyond Nvidia's boardroom. The company's shares have suffered significant losses amid concerns over a possible leadership transition, while stocks of some of its AI ecosystem partners have also come under pressure. Investors fear that a departure could disrupt Nvidia's strategy of financing and supporting companies across the AI supply chain, including data-centre operators and technology firms. Research executives have warned that Huang's personal relationships across the industry have been instrumental in securing major infrastructure deals and investments. His departure could therefore slow the pace of expansion across the AI ecosystem. At the same time, Chinese chipmakers could benefit from the uncertainty if Nvidia's position weakens.A company bigger than its chief executive?Nvidia's extraordinary rise has been closely associated with Huang's personality, vision and leadership. articles.title: Lori Huang, not Jensen, is president of the Huangs’ $9 billion foundation—and co-trustee of the trusts holding most of their Nvidia stake
articles.summary: Nvidia’s board is reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang. Tax and securities filings show his wife of more than 40 years shares control of the family’s fo...
articles.body:
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia , the company announced Thursday . The move follows two extramarital affairs by Huang, one of them with a suspected Chinese spy and another one reportedly with Kimberly Powell , the company's vice president of health care, according to The New York Times .

Huang admitted in a company memo made public on Nov. 8 to extramarital actions: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." Lori has not commented publicly on the memo.

Huang's position has this week raised questions about Nvidia's future, including who would take the reins in his absence, given that he's the face of the $4 trillion chipmaking giant. The board tapped Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

But in the family's philanthropy, his wife, Lori Huang, holds the top title.

Lori is president of the Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation , which reported about $9.2 billion in assets at the end of 2024, according to its most recent tax filing reviewed by Fortune. Jensen is listed as the foundation's secretary and CFO, and Lori has held the president title on every filing available dating back to 2014.

Her role also extends to most of the Huangs' Nvidia shares. As of March 23, Lori and Jensen were co-trustees of three family trusts holding nearly 669 million Nvidia shares, according to Nvidia's latest proxy statement reviewed by Fortune . That's most of the 870.6 million shares (worth roughly $151 billion as of late Nov. 11) the proxy reports as beneficially owned by Jensen, a figure that also includes the foundation's stock.

The proxy also says that as board members of the foundation since 2007, the couple may be deemed to share voting and investment power over its 58.7 million Nvidia shares, though neither has a financial interest in them.

Nvidia's board said Nov. 8 it was investigating reports Jensen had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, but said it "has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised." The independent directors later hired former acting U.S. Attorney Joon H. Kim and his firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to run the probe. China's foreign ministry has called the spying allegations groundless .

Lori, born Lori Mills, met Jensen when the two were paired as lab partners in an electrical fundamentals class at Oregon State University, where she graduated in 1985. He was 17 and she was 19. They married in 1985, and a few years later she left the workforce to raise their two children. Both children, Madison and Spencer, now work at Nvidia. Jensen said in an interview with Singapore-based media outlet CNA that "every moment of Nvidia, she was there."

articles.title: ‘No family dinners’: AMD boss Lisa Su is Jensen Huang’s cousin — with Nvidia on the ropes, is this her time to shine?

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on the fate of Huang , who co-founded the company in 1993. While China has denied U.S. officials' claims that Huang had been secretly having an affair with a woman working for Chinese intelligence, Huang did come clean in a memo to staff that he'd been unfaithful to his wife, sending Nvidia's stock plummeting, losing hundreds of billions worth of market value this week alone.

articles.title: Google knows smart glasses have a privacy problem. Here’s how it’s trying to fix it
articles.summary: Google’s new smart glasses, like Meta’s, light up to show when they’re recording. But once you know someone is recording, what do you do next?
articles.body: Google’s new smart glasses, like Meta’s, light up to show when they’re recording. But once you know someone is recording, what do you do next? That’s one of many key privacy issues Google and other tech companies are under pressure to solve as they bring new AI-powered glasses to market. Google on Thursday announced that the smart glasses it developed with Samsung and eyewear designers Warby Parker and Gentle Monster will launch on December 10. The release comes after Meta’s glasses have caused widespread controversy over their ability to discreetly record others, prompting bans in some venues in cities like New York and London. None of this is lost on Google. The company says its glasses have additional privacy protections, like preventing the glasses from capturing faces when the camera is used to interact with Google’s AI agent, Gemini. But it still hasn’t solved the core privacy problem: Many people are generally uncomfortable with glasses that can record them without their consent, even with an indicator light. And that could present a major blow to the AI ambitions of companies like Google and Meta. Juston Payne, senior director of product management at Google, told CNN the company is looking into new privacy features for its smart glasses, like more ways to alert bystanders when glasses are nearby. But these systems are still in the early research and development phase and may not adequately solve every privacy headache. Smart glasses on the rise Google’s new glasses are meant for easier interactions with Gemini. They have cameras and microphones, which allow users to take photos and videos and speak to Google’s AI agent without taking out their phone. During a demo of the glasses, CNN asked Gemini to suggest a mocktail recipe based on a list of ingredients on a table, for example. The glasses come in styles designed by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, with the former starting at $395 and the latter beginning at $449. “The ability to see the world, hear the world, sense the world around the user, and also have fast real-time interactions with Gemini has always been one of the compelling use cases” for smart glasses, Shahram Izadi, who leads product development and strategy for devices like smart glasses at Google, told CNN. Smart glasses are becoming increasingly popular despite the privacy concerns. Shipments increased by 54% year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026, according to market research firm The International Data Corporation, growing much more quickly than other types of wearable tech like wireless earbuds. EssilorLuxxotica, the eyewear giant that Meta partners with for its glasses, said earlier this year that 7 million pairs of its AI glasses were sold in 2025. Still, many consumers are wary about smart glasses because of the privacy concerns they present, according to Benjamin Chan, an analyst at market research firm ABI Research. Google says its glasses have a tamper-resistant light, along with other protections. When using the camera to ask Gemini questions, the faces of nearby people are redacted before images are sent to Gemini. This only applies to situations when the camera is being used for a Gemini inquiry, not when a user is recording videos or photos to save to their camera roll. Data captured by the camera is encrypted, Google says, and isn’t used for ad targeting or training its models. Apps must also ask for permission before accessing the glasses’ camera. ‘What am I meant to do now?’ The company is researching other privacy measures, Payne told CNN in an interview ahead of the glasses’ launch. There are two areas Google is looking into: more ways to notify users that glasses are nearby, and potential location-based privacy features. Restricting the camera’s functionality based on location would be tricky because the user could potentially work around that by putting their phone in airplane mode, Payne said. And doing so would still likely raise privacy concerns because of how location data is used. The company has also explored a phone notification system for letting people know when the glasses are nearby, similar to third-party apps that already do this. But developing a system that’s actually useful and doesn’t spam users’ phones with notifications is a challenge. And just alerting bystanders doesn’t do much to help, Payne said. “It can actually be weirdly disempowering to you in that you’re like, ‘What am I meant to do now?’” he said. A person might not feel safe asking a stranger to stop recording them, or a worker might not want to confront their boss at the office, said Calli Schroeder, director of the AI and human rights program at the Electronic Privacy Information Center. Privacy experts agree that these challenges exist, but they also say an LED light isn’t sufficient to protect bystanders’ privacy. A visually impaired user wouldn’t be able to see it, for example, and those unfamiliar with the technology may not know what that light means. Izadi pointed out that glasses like Google’s could potentially flag to a visually impaired user whether someone nearby is wearing glasses with the recording light activated. Earlier this year, a report from The New York Times indicating Meta was working on facial recognition for its glasses heightened privacy concerns about the technology. Izadi told CNN that Google has no plans to add facial recognition to its glasses now or in the future. Payne said additional privacy measures are still in the research phase while the company continues to test them. He didn’t provide additional details or release timing. “It’s not to say that we’re not pursuing them,” he said. “We are, we just want to make sure that when they’re rolled out, they’re genuinely robust.”

articles.title: CFO Colette Kress to serve as interim leader after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resignation
articles.summary: Jensen Huang, the founder who propelled Nvidia to become one of the world’s most valuable companies, has resigned from his role as chief executive after 33 years.
articles.body: Jensen Huang, the founder who propelled Nvidia to become one of the world’s most valuable companies, has resigned from his role as chief executive after 33 years. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been appointed interim chief executive, Nvidia’s board said Thursday, as it considers internal and external candidates as a permanent replacement. The announcement ends several days of whirlwind speculation about Huang’s future in the wake of a stunning corporate scandal. “Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, who was also named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair in the Thursday announcement. Jones added that the board expects “the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” Kress will also continue to serve in her current role executive vice president and CFO until Nvidia finds a permanent CEO. As Nvidia’s chief financial officer of more than a decade, Kress has deep knowledge of the business and has been the most visible executive among investors and the public next to Huang. The leadership shakeup came days after the board said it would investigate whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort amid reports of his relationship with a woman US officials believe is a Chinese spy, and shortly after the New York Times reported that the CEO also had an affair with an executive who reports to him. Huang on Sunday admitted to having an extramarital affair, without naming the other party, and apologized to his family and colleagues. The exit marks a sharp fall from grace for Huang, who is largely responsible for kicking off the AI boom. The chips made by the company he founded in 1993 have become critical to the AI infrastructure, putting Nvidia at the center of the AI buildout and thrusting Huang into President Donald Trump’s inner circle. Nvidia shares dropped more than 10% in pre-market trading on Thursday. Nvidia called Huang’s contributions to the company “profound” and thanked him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.” Nvidia’s whirlwind week Huang on Sunday admitted to having an extramarital affair, without naming the other party, and apologized to his family and colleagues. His statement came in tandem with an announcement by the company’s board that it was investigating reports that he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The inquiry followed reports that Huang was in a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen who has worked for Singapore-based tech company and Nvidia customer Megaspeed, whom US officials suspected to be working with Chinese intelligence. The Financial Times reported US officials believed the relationship was romantic in nature. Huang’s ouster represents a quick reversal by the Nvidia board, which initially said it had “confidence” in Huang in its Sunday statement and “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” Trump also defended Huang earlier this week, calling him an “honorable guy.” But the board convened Wednesday night to weigh whether to oust Huang following the New York Times report about his additional affair with a company executive. Huang’s influence at Nvidia Huang has transformed Nvidia into much more than a chipmaker, but the centerpiece of the AI revolution. He was early to bet that graphics processing units – chips commonly used in video game consoles – would be critical for training AI models. Now, Nvidia offers all the pieces needed for AI computing, from models catered to specific industries like robotics and data centers to networking technology, boosting it to become the world’s first $ trillion company last year. Clad in his signature leather jacket, Huang himself became an icon of the AI boom – drawing major crowds at the company’s conferences and other tech events. Some have viewed him with rockstar-like reverence; a woman once asked him to sign her chest during an autograph session at a tech conference in Taiwan. Tech companies like Google have developed their own chips, in part to reduce their reliance on Nvidia. But Huang’s company is largely unmatched in the AI chips race. “If you look at the magnitude of Nvidia’s offerings, nobody really can touch them,” Ted Mortonson, technology desk sector strategist at Baird, told CNN last year. As Nvidia’s profile has grown, so has Huang’s: His close relationship with Trump has given him influence in AI policy decisions. Trump even recently called Huang when he was in the middle of giving a talk at a conference in September, which the Nvidia CEO put on speaker for the crowd to hear. Huang had become synonymous with Nvidia, and his ouster casts one of the world’s largest and most influential companies into a period of uncertainty. There’s never been an Nvidia without Huang; he told Bloomberg in 2023 that the company “was built so that I know how to run it.” This story has been updated with additional details and context.

articles.title: Wall Street today: Nvidia tumbles 12% in pre-market trading as Jensen Huang steps down as CEO
articles.summary: US stock futures slid on Thursday as Nvidia shares plunged over 12% after Jensen Huang stepped down as the chipmaker’s CEO, triggering a broader sell-off
articles.body: US stock futures slid on Thursday as Nvidia shares plunged over 12% after Jensen Huang stepped down as the chipmaker’s CEO, triggering a broader sell-off in artificial intelligence-linked stocks. The leadership shake-up at the $4 trillion company rattled investor sentiment, adding to concerns over an AI sector already grappling with funding uncertainties and regulatory scrutiny.Dow futures edged down 23 points, or 0.04%, to 52,555, while S&P 500 futures shed 43.75 points, or 0.57%, to 7,596.75. Nasdaq futures led the losses, falling 352.25 points, or 1.24%, to 28,121, as Nvidia shares plunged 12.50%.Nvidia's board had met on Wednesday to discuss Huang's position after allegations that the 63-year-old had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing. Reports also alleged that he had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him.The controversy has raised concerns about the future of the $4 trillion chipmaker and the wider AI ecosystem, which Huang helped build by directing Nvidia's growing cash reserves towards cloud providers, suppliers and major research laboratories. The company's practice of financing infrastructure built around its chips has also attracted scrutiny over circular funding.Other AI stocks fall tooThe sell-off spread across AI-linked companies, with Oracle shares falling 3%, Micron Technology dropping nearly 5% and Intel declining more than 3%. Neocloud company Nebius fell 13% in premarket trading despite reporting better-than-expected third-quarter revenue, as its guidance disappointed investors. Advanced Micro Devices, however, moved higher after receiving an upgrade from William Blair.In Hong Kong, Alibaba and Tencent fell 6.7% and 2.6%, respectively, amid concerns that Washington could restrict access to offshore data centres equipped with advanced processors. Meanwhile, Chinese domestic GPU makers gained as investors anticipated that Nvidia's troubles could help local suppliers capture a larger market share.Dollar, bond yields add to market pressureThe Nvidia developments added to broader global market uncertainty. The dollar touched a 19-month high, while the US 10-year Treasury yield climbed back to 5% amid growing expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike next month.The dollar has gained more than 1.5% since stronger-than-expected US inflation data prompted investors to reassess interest rate expectations. According to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, traders are now pricing in a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike, compared with a one-in-three chance of rates remaining unchanged a week ago.Meanwhile, Brent crude climbed above $92 a barrel as Middle East tensions offset rising regional output. US President Donald Trump added to uncertainty after saying in a Truth Social post, "We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed."Nvidia in focusAs Jensen Huang steps down, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO following Jensen Huang's departure, the chipmaker said on Thursday. She will lead the company while it searches for a permanent successor.Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 as executive vice-president and chief financial officer and has held the position since. During her tenure, the company's revenue grew from $4.13 billion in the fiscal year she joined to $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026, reflecting Nvidia's massive business expansion.She has also regularly joined Huang on the company's quarterly earnings calls, where Nvidia discusses its financial performance and outlook. Her appointment brings a long-serving finance executive to the helm of the chipmaker, whose processors are widely used in advanced computing systems and artificial intelligence data centres.Investors are now looking towards Nvidia's earnings next Tuesday for further cues on the AI trade. Saxo Bank's Chief Investment Strategist Charu Chanana said, "Strong results could reaffirm the AI growth story, but may not fully remove the governance discount."Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer at Longbow Asset Management, said the controversy could weigh on the company."I believe the board won't oust him until they have an all-star, a known entity in the tech sector, to replace him," he said. "At the end of the day, let's not forget that the Nvidia chip is the centrepiece of the AI story."Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Qualcomm CEO on tech stock meltdown: 'There is no AI correction' for us
articles.summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon is staying bullish on his prospects despite the tech stock meltdown.
articles.body:
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) CEO Cristiano Amon doesn't think his tech giant should be lumped in with other AI stocks recently being dumped hand over fist.

"We're new to the data center, so all of these things don't really apply to us. There is no AI correction in Qualcomm," Amon said at Yahoo Finance Invest when asked about the tech stock rout following the midterm elections .

"We are just starting on our journey on the data center," he added. "But here's one thing that is important to look at. When I look at the semiconductor industry today, it's on an extreme shortage. We're short on wafers, we're short on substrate, we're short on assembly. Everything is short because demand is very, very high. The second thing is everybody talks about it. In some cases, you have energy lead times that sometimes are not the same as the compute lead time. And sometimes energy projects take you longer. So I think there may be a disconnect in what the market probably expects on the rate of build-out and the actual rate of build-out, which is probably paced by energy and supply."

The markets remain on high alert amid fears that a slowdown in data center build-outs will upset the profit boom of the world's biggest companies — all of which are in tech.

Those fears have been amplified in the wake of the blue wave that erupted on Election Day, which could see newly elected Democratic senators and governors muck up the AI expansion.

This led to a historic and painful session for investors on Nov. 5.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost 4.4% of its market value , wiping out $3 trillion in the process.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) plunged 1,280 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) cratered 4.8%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ).

Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially tech names.

Qualcomm isn't exactly 100% immune from the AI infrastructure risk-off trade.

The company is aggressively pushing into the US data center build-out by positioning itself as a power-efficient alternative to AI chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ), specifically targeting large-scale AI inference workloads with its new Dragonfly architecture and high-bandwidth compute platforms.

Qualcomm said in early September that hyperscaler Amazon ( AMZN ) ‌could buy up to $60 billion of its AI data center chips and related products under a long-term partnership.

On the market dynamics, Amon added, "I think the market is probably getting to the realization of what exactly the speed of build-out which is available by the supply of the industry. And look, it's very high volatility right now. So it's really difficult to have a precise opinion on this. And what I said coming back to Qualcomm is we're new to this, we're being modest, and for everything that I outlined out there, I have the supply, I have the demand."

articles.title: Warsh discloses wife’s transactions related to pet care investment firm
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh disclosed transactions his wife made related to a company that invests in pet care. Warsh reported to the U.S. Office of Government Ethics (OGE) six equity and warrant purchases in TAW LLC in August and September. A Fed spokesperson told The Hill that Warsh’s wife, Jane Lauder, made the transactions.…
articles.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh disclosed transactions his wife made related to a company that invests in pet care.

Warsh reported to the U.S. Office of Government Ethics (OGE) six equity and warrant purchases in TAW LLC in August and September. A Fed spokesperson told The Hill that Warsh’s wife, Jane Lauder, made the transactions.

The disclosure forms released Wednesday by the OGE valued the transactions, which included four purchases of equity and a warrant and two purchases of future equity and a warrant, at between $400,000 and $900,000.

The Fed spokesperson noted central bank officials must report transactions involving spouses.

Lauder, the billionaire daughter of businessman and diplomat Ronald Lauder, founded TAW Ventures after her goldendoodle, Thaddeus, suffered “a series of unexplained episodes,” she said on the company’s website .

“Through my own extensive research, I came to believe these episodes were likely triggered by a common preventive medication prescribed by many vets,” Lauder added. “Thankfully, since removing it, Thaddeus has returned to his happy, healthy self.”

TAW Ventures’s portfolio includes dog food and treat companies, a pet medicine firm and a veterinary dental practice. Lauder’s equity and warrant purchases in TAW LLC included investments in multiple companies within its portfolio, per the ethics forms.

Multiple OGE officials approved the transactions, the forms noted.

Warsh, the wealthiest Fed chair in history, has led the central bank since May, after President Trump nominated him to succeed former Chair Jerome Powell.

Prior to his Senate confirmation hearing in April, Warsh disclosed assets valued at between $131 million and $209 million to the OGE.

The Fed strengthened its ethics rules in 2022 after multiple officials disclosed stock trades . Under the requirements, senior central bank officials cannot purchase individual stocks or sector funds, holding investments in bonds or cryptocurrencies, among other assets.

articles.title: Nvidia stock falls after Huang resigns, weighing on broader market
articles.summary: Stocks declined at the opening bell on news that Jensen Huang, one of the most important executives in the AI boom, resigned as CEO of Nvidia.
articles.body: Major stock indexes declined at the opening bell on news that Jensen Huang, one of the most important executives in the AI boom, was resigning effective immediately as CEO of Nvidia. After diving 12% at the open, Nvidia was down more than 4% as of early Thursday afternoon, as the company and investors grappled with multiple scandals that have engulfed its co-founder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang. Throughout the day, the company was among the biggest decliners on the Nasdaq, Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 indexes. Major indexes also faced choppy trading. All three were slightly higher after following a similar pattern to Nvidia’s: falling, rising and then declining again. Without a formal succession plan, the company that designs the chips powering the entire AI sector was thrust into crisis. It’s a pivotal moment for AI, with Anthropic gearing up for its potentially trillion-dollar-plus initial public offering next week. Anthropic is highly reliant on Nvidia’s chips and has entered into hundreds of billions of dollars worth of contracts with cloud providers to rent them. Nvidia named its longtime chief financial officer as its interim leader. Huang’s departure from Nvidia came after a New York Times report said the CEO had had a relationship with an executive at Nvidia who reports to him. That came right on the heels of his admission Sunday that he was “unfaithful” to his wife, an announcement that was released after the Financial Times reported Saturday that Huang had had a relationship with a businesswoman whom a source told NBC News was a Chinese spy. There are few companies as important to the artificial intelligence industry as Nvidia. “We’re probably the only AI company in the world that works with every AI company in the world,” Huang told Bloomberg in an October interview. As reports swirled around Huang this week, Nvidia’s shares have plunged, erasing about $515 billion in value. Nvidia’s total market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025 in early trading. The news surrounding Huang, a confidant of President Donald Trump’s, also raises the prospect of tighter regulations on the chip and AI industry, which could further pressure stock indexes that have been powered for years by the explosion in AI stocks. “All told, given the national security concerns, we think the risk of more restrictive guidelines on shipments directly or indirectly into China has risen,” JPMorgan analysts said Thursday before Huang was removed. Industry experts widely believe that American leadership in AI has been powered by Nvidia. That too could come into question. “We expect the [Nvidia] team to maintain its leadership in AI,” JPMorgan’s team said, while cautioning that “history has shown that one execution misstep often leads to more.” “Maintaining flawless execution” will be critical to Nvidia and the sector going forward, they said. Also pressuring stock indexes was news from AI cloud startup Nebius, which reported that it beat earnings expectations. But the company also gave investors disappointing guidance. Investors have been on edge about AI-linked firms, especially smaller startups, given that they require tens of billions of dollars to get their data centers up and running. Overall, the sector has poured hundreds of billions of dollars into developing AI systems, data centers and equipment, but investors remain nervous about how soon those investments could pay off. Nebius shares plummeted almost 20%. Its peer CoreWeave also fell 10% after surging Wednesday. Together, the Nvidia and Nebius news sent the entire tech sector lower, and it was the worst performing S&P sector Thursday. Suppliers to both companies also fell. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 2%, while an ETF that tracks memory suppliers fell 4%.

articles.title: 'A tough market': Home sales fall to lowest level since 2010 as high mortgage rates paralyze activity
articles.summary: Home sales dropped sharply in October as mortgage rates above 7% paralyzed the market.
articles.body:
Home sales in October hit their lowest level since the aftermath of the mortgage crisis as mortgage rates averaged well above 7%.

Existing home sales dropped 5.5% from a month earlier and 8.8% from October 2025 to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of just 3.75 million homes, according to National Association of Realtors data released on Thursday. Sales haven't been that slow since August 2010, when the housing market was still recovering from the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis.

"It is just a tough market for buyers and sellers trying to get that transaction," NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun said.

Mortgage rates crossed 7% in September, but their chilling effect on home sales was slightly delayed. Homes typically go under contract a month or two before they're sold, meaning that many of September's buyers could have locked in rates below 7%, while those in October weren't so lucky.

Sales dropped throughout the country, with the West seeing a particularly steep 14.5% year-over-year decline. Even the Northeast, home to many of the nation's hottest housing markets, saw home sales fall 4.1% from last year.

The dismal October data and the fact that mortgage rates have stayed above 7% mean home sales this year are likely to come in below 2025's level of 4.06 million, reaching a more than three-decade low, Yun said.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?
articles.summary: Nvidia CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO following Jensen Huang's ouster.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO after Jensen Huang stepped down amid allegations of an affair with a Chinese spy and a company executive.

Kress, one of Nvidia's more prominent executives, joined the company in 2013 and helped guide its financial success, transforming it from a video game company into the AI juggernaut it is today.

In a statement, Kress said she is committed to building on the work Jensen has done to turn Nvidia into the company it has become.

"We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders," she said.

3 challenges for a post-Jensen Huang Nvidia

Wall Street backs away from Nvidia as Jensen Huang uncertainty unfolds: What analysts are saying

Kress regularly provides financial updates during Nvidia's quarterly earnings call, making her well-known among analysts and investors.

Prior to joining the company, Kress served as senior vice president and CFO for Cisco's ( CSCO ) Business Technology and Operations Finance group, according to her Nvidia biography .

Before joining Cisco, she held positions at Microsoft ( MSFT ) for 13 years, including as CFO of the company's Server and Tools group. She also worked at Texas Instruments ( TXN ) in several roles.

"Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," newly appointed Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.

"She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," he added.

Kress succeeds Huang, who is embroiled in two alleged affairs: one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell .

On Sunday, Huang issued a statement admitting to the initial affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees.

According to reports, the woman Huang was seeing, Alice Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based technology firm MegaSpeed and was allegedly acting as a spy on behalf of the Chinese government.

Nvidia's board has said it has launched an independent investigation into the matter, but added it has no reason to believe Nvidia trade secrets or national security were compromised.

articles.title: Jensen Huang exits Nvidia: What it means for the AI market, investors
articles.summary: Jensen Huang’s exit as Nvidia boss has added to uncertainty to an already nervous AI market.
articles.body: Jensen Huang’s exit as Nvidia boss has added to uncertainty to an already nervous AI market.For months, investors have been questioning whether the AI boom is turning into a bubble. The exit of CEO Jensen Huang has raised fresh concerns about the future of the artificial intelligence bellwether.Nvidia shares plunged 13% at the opening bell, taking the company's market value below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025. The fall dragged whole of the Wall Street in red with Dow Jones Industrial Average slipping 50.01 points, or 0.10%, to 52,436.48. The Nasdaq Composite fell 169.62 points, or 0.67%, to 25,296.57, while the S&P 500 declined 37.68 points, or 0.49%, to 7,581.70.The fall comes as investors try to understand what Huang's departure could mean for Nvidia's business, its position in the AI industry and the wider technology market.Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and turned it into one of the biggest players in the AI industry, is stepping down as CEO. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO while the company looks for a permanent successor, Nvidia said on Thursday.Huang, who owns about 3.61% of the company and is its fourth-largest investor, will also step down from the board.AI market loses one of its biggest championsHuang's exit is significant because his influence went beyond Nvidia. He was one of the most prominent faces of the AI boom, and his departure has left investors wondering whether the leadership change could affect the company's growth and the wider AI industry.Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, UK, said investors were still trying to understand what the change meant for Nvidia."Investors are trying to figure out what it means exactly for the future of the company. They're putting someone as an interim just to step in. It's just a concern about what the leadership transition means for the company, whether it changes much.”The expert further told Reuters, "There's a key risk here because Jensen was seen as the kind of the front man of AI, not just at Nvidia, but in general. And him stepping down kind of adds a little bit of jitters to the market ahead of the earnings next week and obviously in the middle of this AI rout that we're going through. So it's just adds another layer of that kind of uncertainty and concern being piled onto the market."The timing is also important, with Nvidia's earnings due next week. Investors are now weighing the leadership change alongside existing concerns about the AI market.Will AI companies feel the heatNvidia's role in the AI industry is not limited to selling chips. Its business ties with several companies have also raised questions about how smaller players could be affected if the chipmaker changes its approach.Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, said Nvidia's role in the industry makes its next steps important for companies that depend on it."Nvidia has been called the 'Bank of AI.' They'll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what's going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That's an open question."The supply of chips is another concern. If other chipmakers can meet demand, companies may still be able to continue building data centres and investing in AI. But a shortage could create problems for the industry."I have heard from some data-center folks that they can buy chips from other companies as long as those companies can supply them. If that's the case, the AI trade continues, companies keep building data centers, and life goes on. But if there's a supply shortage, then you have a problem."What happens to the AI boomHuang's departure has also raised questions about whether the pace of AI development could change. Concerns over how quickly the technology is advancing and whether enough controls are in place have already been raised by Congress and others.Saluzzi told Reuters that the development could slow the industry down and give companies and policymakers time to take stock."It could also simply slow down the AI machine. Congress and others have raised concerns about the speed of AI development and whether there are proper controls and regulations. Maybe something like this slows it down, lets everyone take a breath, and acts as a kind of regulation without a regulation."Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, Connecticut, said the news was difficult for Nvidia and the wider technology market, given how much the AI industry's expansion depends on the company's chips."It's very difficult to spin this as good news for NVIDIA. It's difficult for the tech trade right now because not only is NVIDIA's technology so central to the AI build out, but if this puts a damper on their ability to generate cash flow at the same rate they always have, that becomes tricky."Sosnick also pointed to Nvidia's many business arrangements across the industry. He said these ties had raised questions about whether they had made the AI market more stable or more fragile."The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question into whether that created more stability or more fragility ... There'll be investigations. The Republicans may not investigate so much, but when you have a new Democratic Congress, I'm sure there will be all sorts of investigations as to whether export controls were violated, whether this was done with the knowledge of the, Department of Commerce and what the State Department knew about this."Should Nvidia investors worryFor investors, much will depend on how smoothly Nvidia manages the leadership change and whether it can maintain its business momentum.Colette Kress, who is taking over as interim CEO, is well regarded by investors. However, the challenge is significant, given that Nvidia has been led by its founder since the company was set up.Gil Luria, managing director at DA Davidson, Portland, said Kress should be able to steer the company through the transition, but Huang's exit leaves a big gap in decision-making."Colette Kress is well respected by investors and should be able to guide NVIDIA through this challenging period. The task is daunting, as NVIDIA has been founder-led since inception and Mr. Huang concentrated much of the decision making," Luria said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nvidia stock falls nearly 15 percent after Huang resigns
articles.summary: Nvidia stock took a sharp dive on Thursday, after longtime CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid reports he engaged in two extramarital affairs. The chipmaker’s stock fell to $148.80 per share after the opening bell, down 14.4 percent from closing on Wednesday. Nvidia stock later rebounded slightly, topping $162 per share, but it was down about…
articles.body:
Nvidia stock took a sharp dive on Thursday, after longtime CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid reports he engaged in two extramarital affairs.

The chipmaker’s stock fell to $148.80 per share after the opening bell, down 14.4 percent from closing on Wednesday.

Nvidia stock later rebounded slightly, topping $162 per share, but it was down about 8 percent as of the initial 45 minutes of trading.

The tech giant’s board of directors announced Huang’s resignation on Thursday, after The New York Times reported that he had two affairs — including one with a woman, Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy.

The board of directors thanked Jensen Huang in a statement , calling his contributions to the company “profound.”

The board added, “NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.”

Huang’s resignation came a day after the Times reported on another affair he had with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare.

Colette Kress, Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer since 2013, will serve as interim CEO, the board noted. Kress said in the statement she is “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created” since he founded Nvidia in 1993.

“We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders,” Kress said.

Lawmakers on Capitol Hill have scrutinized Nvidia and Huang after the Times reported on his affair with Alice Huang.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), set to chair the Senate Banking Committee come January, said Thursday that Jensen Huang and Nvidia board members “still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance” with U.S. export controls.

“It’s clear that the American people cannot rely on Big Tech billionaire CEOs to put our national security above their bottom line,” Warren added.

articles.title: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman explains the 'paradox' of AI for his company
articles.summary: While AI may be the future, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman sees his company as powered by humans.
articles.body:
Reddit ( RDDT ) is one of the most frequently cited sources in AI-generated answers. Yet its most recent earnings report showed that Google's AI Overviews have undermined its search traffic.

At Yahoo Finance Invest , Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman described this dynamic as the "paradox" of AI for the company.

"AI does not exist as we know it without Reddit, " Huffman said on Thursday. "Every model you've heard of trained with or without our permission using Reddit. It's this paradox which is the more AI there is, the more the human nature of Reddit stands out."

In a quarterly letter to investors in October, Huffman noted that Reddit's search traffic "dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week" during the month. "Web search is evolving from a gateway to the web to becoming an AI-powered destination itself," Huffman said.

Huffman added in the company's third quarter earnings call that "Google is not sending [users] to Reddit the way they used to."

According to Similarweb, a web analytics platform, Reddit's traffic is down 13% year over year. Reddit's $60 million-a-year data deal with Google is up for renewal next year.

The company's Q3 report showed total daily active unique users increased 12% year over year to 130.3 million (slightly below analyst expectations of 133.7 million), while US daily active users declined 2% year over year. While the company beat earnings per share estimates, it came up short on its Q4 revenue forecast, predicting sales of $1.0 billion to $1.03 billion (slightly below some Wall Street consensus estimates near $1.05 billion).

Huffman told Yahoo Finance that Reddit will begin testing a requirement for users to log in to access content on the platform in the United States starting this quarter.

"We are not the first," Huffman said, speaking about other social media platforms. "In fact, we are quite literally the last company to go through this transition." He added that the company, however, does not want to wall itself off from the open web — whether that's humans or AI.

The ethos driving Reddit, Huffman explained, is that "Reddit is for humans." The platform is all about "questions that have no answers."

"'What should I watch tonight?' There's not a factual answer for that — there's just 100 answers. And all of those answers have a different point of view and context," Huffman said. "People like the different perspectives. They like the mess. They like the chaos — that's what being human is."

articles.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia ousting may signal shifting winds on China in Washington
articles.summary: The Jensen Huang saga could open a window for China hawks on the Hill to press their case.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang's ouster from the top of Nvidia ( NVDA ), the world's leading chipmaker, could portend a broader shift in Washington over China's access to Silicon Valley's most advanced chips.

Though concerns around China's ambitions to catch up to US progress on AI have long existed on the Hill, those worries were blown into much wider focus last week after the New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with a Chinese national named Alice Huang, who the US intelligence service reportedly believes has committed espionage on behalf of Beijing.

Huang will soon face questions in Washington about his company's approach to AI. Representative Brian Mast (R-Fla.) told reporters in a briefing on Thursday that the former Nvidia CEO has agreed to appear before Congress after Mast and fellow Representatives John Moolenaar (R-Mich.) and Rick Crawford (R-Ark.) sent a letter to Huang last week requesting his presence at a closed-door hearing on the Hill.

That hearing has been scheduled for Nov. 18, the day after Nvidia is set to report earnings on Nov. 17. Mast had expressed willingness to issue a subpoena to Huang if no response is received, which would have compelled Huang to testify had he not agreed voluntarily.

Huang has been highly visible in President Trump's circle over the past year, meeting the president in Alaska to be picked up on Air Force One for Trump's most recent trip to China and then sitting with his wife at the head table of President Trump's state summit dinner in September hosted for Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

"NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has spent years lobbying Trump to allow advanced AI chip sales to China," Sen. Chris Coons (D-Del.), said on Thursday. "Now, serious questions are emerging about his ties to an alleged Chinese spy and what Trump knew. Congress needs answers, and Americans deserve better national security protections."

The scandal has also raised much wider questions in Washington about the future of US-China AI relations, including the potential passage of several pieces of legislation that would seek to clamp down on China's access to US silicon.

Though the Commerce Department has blocked Nvidia from selling the newest versions of its chips to Chinese firms since 2022 as Washington fights to maintain a competitive edge over Beijing, Huang secured permission from the White House in December 2025 to export its H200 chips to Chinese buyers.

Since the US government imposed its sales restrictions on Nvidia, public reporting and investigations by the Department of Justice have documented a black-market shadow trade. Users on Douyin, the nation's version of TikTok — which is only accessible on phones with Chinese SIM cards — openly offer sales of sanctioned chips such as Nvidia's Blackwell B300 in videos reviewed by Yahoo Finance.

articles.summary: DoubleLine founder Jeffrey Gundlach is still sitting out the AI stock dance.
articles.body:
DoubleLine founder Jeffrey Gundlach is still sitting out the AI stock dance, even with the sector having been crushed under the weight of its own expectations and the Election Day blue wave.

"So what we've been really focusing on is avoiding what I've been calling, ever since about September, the blast radius of all of this," the well-known bond king said at Yahoo Finance Invest . "Where you don't want to own the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ), you don't want to own any cap-weighted index. You don't want to invest in an index fund that's cap-weighted because you're getting tremendous concentration of about 60% — well, it depends what statistics you look at, but something like half of the market is in this AI and AI-adjacent stuff."

Fears about the health of the AI trade have quickly come into focus in the wake of the blue wave that erupted on Election Day , which could see newly elected Democratic senators and governors muck up the AI expansion.

This led to a historic — and brutal — session for investors on Nov. 5.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost 4.4% of its market value , wiping out $3 trillion in the process.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) plunged 1,280 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) cratered 4.8%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ).

Stocks continued to trade with a downward bias, especially tech names. Not helping sentiment is Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's resignation following his high-profile affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and fellow Nvidia executive.

Nvidia technology and financial commitments are the epicenter of the AI boom. Any disruption to either is the last thing AI investors want to see right now.

articles.body:
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) will price its initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday, Nov. 18, the company announced Thursday .

It will begin trading under the ticker symbol "ANT" on Thursday, Nov. 19.

The company, which publicly filed its S-1 investor prospectus late last month, will provide the next major test for the AI trade and could set the standard for rival OpenAI's own public markets debut, which is anticipated for early next year.

In an amended S-1 filing released Tuesday , Anthropic said it expects to sell 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78. That would give the company a market valuation of between $1.3 trillion and $1.45 trillion.

Anthropic was initially projected to hit the market with a valuation as high as $2 trillion, but recent market turmoil in the AI sector has knocked that down significantly.

For the first nine months of the year ending Sept. 30, Anthropic said revenue grew $1,206% to $33.2 billion.

The company's original S-1 , which covered the first six months of the year through June 30, listed revenue of $16.3 billion. Anthropic recorded revenue of $4.6 billion in all of 2025.

Operating losses also improved year over year, coming in at $1.3 billion in the first nine months of the year, down from $5.2 billion in the same period last year.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of $536 million in the September quarter, compared with operating income of $974 million in the June quarter.

The company says the decline is the result of a $5 billion charge for compute under short-term commitments, as well as $2 billion in non-cash charges from its donation matching program.

The AI giant also revealed a staggering aggregate committed spend of $895.4 billion , which it says is primarily related to compute and infrastructure.
