articles.title: Democrats’ mandate: Make billionaires pay their fair share into Social Security
articles.summary: Following their success in the 2026 midterms, Democrats are being urged to pass the Social Security Expansion Act to eliminate funding shortfalls and require the wealthy to pay their fair share.
articles.body:
Minimum wage workers contribute a vastly higher percentage of their income to Social Security than billionaires. That’s because all workers, even millionaires and billionaires, stop paying into Social Security after their first $184,500 in earnings . Unearned investment income, which is how Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and other billionaires make most of their money, isn’t subject to Social Security taxes at all.

In the 2026 midterm elections, Democrats ran on a promise to make the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share. From Texas to Maine to South Carolina to Iowa and beyond, Democrats pledged to “scrap the cap” on Social Security contributions so that the wealthy pay the same rate as minimum wage workers. Voters responded by giving Democrats a resounding victory, and the opportunity to act on that promise.

This was the affordability election, and Social Security is a key affordability issue. It ensures that Americans have a measure of protection when they retire, become disabled, or lose a family breadwinner. Benefits are modest but essential, not just to those who receive them but also to their families. Over six million children either receive benefits directly or live with someone who does.

Social Security faces a funding shortfall, which will result in an over 20 percent benefit cut in 2032 if Congress does not act. Rather than waiting until the last possible minute, Democrats should give the American people peace of mind about their essential earned benefits by passing legislation next year that not only eliminates the shortfall but expands benefits both across-the-board and in targeted ways.

Fortunately, Democrats have already crafted several pieces of legislation that fit the moment and have been introduced in the current Congress. One of them, the Social Security Expansion Act , would increase benefits by $200 a month and ensure that all benefits can be paid in full and on time. It is fully funded by requiring the wealthy to pay in on all of their income, including unearned investment income.

The Social Security Expansion Act is sponsored by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), who is going to chair the Senate Finance Committee’s Social Security Subcommittee in the next Congress. After the election, Sanders wrote that he intends to make passing it into law a top priority . That is the right thing to do.

Holding a vote on the Social Security Expansion Act would allow Democrats to show their constituents that they are serious about protecting their benefits and making the uber-wealthy pay their fair share. The mainstream media would no longer be able to inaccurately state that “Congress” is doing nothing on the issue, disguising the striking difference between the two parties. Voting on Social Security legislation would also force every member of Congress on the record.

Poll after poll has found that Democratic, Republican and independent voters alike want to protect and expand Social Security by making the wealthy pay their fair share. In contrast, Republican politicians claim that they “love” Social Security, but advocate benefit cuts , often using oblique language, such as arguing for the need to “fix” Social Security. If Republicans are forced to vote, they will find themselves squeezed between their constituents and their billionaire donors.

Regardless of the outcome, a vote is a win for Democrats. It either results in the enactment of important legislation or makes the radical desire of Republican politicians to side with billionaires clear, and gives Democrats a winning issue to run on in 2028.

Democrats must not waver. In recent months, a handful of Republicans have begun talking about lifting the cap on Social Security contributions, realizing the policy’s overwhelming popularity. That’s good news. But a deal that modifies the cap, while also cutting benefits, is not what Americans voted for.

Billionaires and the interest groups they fund are pushing hard for a so-called “balanced package” that keeps most billionaire earnings exempt from Social Security contributions. Such a package might include some revenue, but also catastrophic benefit cuts. It is essential that Democrats resist that pressure and side with the overwhelming majority of Americans who don’t want a single penny of cuts to Social Security.

Benefits are already too low. Any cuts would force millions of retirees, widows, widowers, people with disabilities, and their families into poverty. Many would lose the roofs over their heads and the food on their tables. Instead, we should expand Social Security and improve the financial security of families across the country.

In 1932, America faced destructive and immoral levels of income and wealth inequality, just as we do today. Voters responded to the Great Depression by sweeping Franklin D. Roosevelt and the Democratic Party into power. Roosevelt and his fellow Democrats responded by creating Social Security, the most successful and most beloved social program the country has ever seen.

Just like during the Great Depression, many Americans are now unable to afford life’s basic necessities. Once again, they have elected Democrats to resolve that crisis. Democrats should respond by expanding Social Security for generations to come.

Nancy Altman is president of Social Security Works.

articles.title: House Republican says Huang has agreed to appear before lawmakers

articles.body:
Jensen Huang, the tech executive at the center of an alleged Chinese corporate espionage scandal, has agreed to appear before Congress in a closed-door briefing focused on threats to U.S. national security , a top Republican told The Hill on Thursday.

Rep. Brian Mast (R-Fla.), the chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said lawmakers are negotiating the timing of Huang’s appearance. Mast, along with the top Republicans on the Intelligence Committee and Select Committee on the China, sent a letter to Huang last week asking him to respond by Nov. 11 to a request to appear before Congress.

“We’re in negotiations for which day, which attorneys, his personnel,” Mast said.

“It’s likely going to be under oath, transcribed, video recorded between several committees. Certainly Intel, China Select, and Foreign Affairs will likely be there for sure,” Mast added.

Rep. John Moolenaar (R-Mich.) is the chair of the House Select Committee on China, and Rep. Rick Crawford (R-Ark.) is the chair of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

Huang announced Thursday his resignation as the head of his company Nvidia only a few days after he admitted to two extramarital affairs. The first reported affair was with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, The New York Times reported.

Nvidia is one of America’s largest companies and a manufacturer of advanced semiconductor chips heavily sought after by China. Huang has been an advocate for permitting sales to China as lawmakers hawkish on the threats from Beijing called for greater restrictions on chip sales.

articles.title: Bodhi Tree to invest $180 million for a majority stake in Adyar Ananda Bhavan
articles.summary: CHENNAI: In one of the largest deals in the Indian restaurant sector, Bodhi Tree System (BTS) announced a $180 million investment for an undisclosed
articles.body: CHENNAI: In one of the largest deals in the Indian restaurant sector, Bodhi Tree System (BTS) announced a $180 million investment for an undisclosed majority stake in leading south-based vegetarian restaurant chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B).The investment by BTS, an investor-operator platform co-founded by media veterans James Murdoch and Uday Shankar, is aimed at expanding the footprint of the Chennai-based brand in domestic and international markets, according to a statement.At present, A2B operates 160 outlets, largely in southern states such as Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and Puducherry, and 30 outlets globally, including in Singapore, the US, Australia and Malaysia.Uday Shankar will serve as chairperson of A2B’s new board of directors. Industry sources said discussions over the tie-up had been going on for more than a year. “It is a joint venture between the two companies, wherein A2B co-founders and brothers K T Srinivasa Raja and K T Venkatesan will offer their guidance. The duo has a significant say in this partnership,” a source familiar with the developments said.The deal is expected to strengthen A2B’s leadership and talent pool, build digital capabilities, modernise its kitchens, bring manufacturing up to global standards, expand its range of healthy and nutritious food, and grow its restaurant and packaged-food businesses across India and international markets.Veda Corporate Advisors was the exclusive financial adviser to A2B.James Murdoch and Uday Shankar said A2B was a formidable brand in India and that they looked forward to working with the team to take its authentic cuisine to a far broader global audience. A2B’s co-founders said the plan they had built together would make A2B a company fit for the public markets, allowing customers, employees and investors to share in its future.A2B has operated under several names over the years and traces its roots to Rajapalayam in Virudhunagar district. The founders’ father, K S Thirupathi Raja, started a small sweet stall named Sri Guru Sweets in Rajapalayam in the 1960s. He later moved to Bengaluru in 1975, where he operated a sweet stall under the name Sri Srinivasa Sweets. Thirupathi Raja returned to Tamil Nadu to launch Sri Ananda Bhavan Sweets in Washermenpet, north Chennai, in 1980. However, the name changed to Adyar Ananda Bhavan when the business reached the Adyar locality in the late 1980s.From sweets and savouries to chaats and snacks, the premium eatery went on to introduce multi-cuisine dishes on its menu. articles.title: 65% of manufacturing investment commitments at 2025 GIM converted: Patil
articles.summary: Karnataka says 65% of 2025 Global Investors Meet manufacturing commitments converted; 2027 GIM set for Apr 20-22 as state pushes projects and approvals.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Around 65% of the manufacturing investment commitments secured at Karnataka’s 2025 Global Investors Meet have been converted into projects, large and medium industries minister M B Patil said on Thursday.Speaking at the curtain-raiser for the 2027 edition of Global Investors Meet in Bengaluru, Patil said the previous edition had attracted investment commitments of Rs 10.3 lakh crore across sectors. The next meet will be held at Bangalore Palace from April 20 to 22.He said cl. Land had also been allotted to companies such as Lam Research and Applied Materials, he said.Chief minister D K Shivakumar said the state’s power expansion plans would require investments of more than Rs 3 lakh crore over the next five years. He reiterated the govt’s plan to invest over Rs 1.5 lakh crore in Bengaluru’s infrastructure, including mobility and water projects, and said efforts were under way to resolve delays faced by investors.Patil said the state would organise a dedicated investors’ conclave for North Karnataka in the coming months, apart from domestic and international roadshows ahead of the global meet.“We want this region to attract investment at a scale it has never seen before,” he said.He said the govt had acted on more than 35 of the 55 suggestions made during consultations with industry. Measures to facilitate investments included a digital industrial land bank, dedicated officers to assist investors and affidavit-based clearances that allow eligible investors to begin work while approvals are being processed.Deputy chief minister G Parameshwara said 147 industrial projects involving investments of Rs 6,826 crore had received approvals this week. Of these, 131 were proposed outside Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts. He also pitched Tumakuru as a manufacturing destination, citing its proximity to Bengaluru’s talent pool, availability of land and industrial infrastructure.Policy initiatives highlighted at the event included support for the aerospace and defence sectors, additional capital subsidies for emerging industries in industrially backward regions and housing for workers near factories.Plans for the 2027 meet include a supplier event to connect manufacturers with potential suppliers, country-specific roundtables and the third edition of Venturise, the startup-focused event.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: CoreWeave stock sinks as resignation of Jensen Huang ripples through AI trade
articles.summary: CoreWeave stock sank on Thursday as the impact of leadership change at Nvidia weighed on the AI trade and companies backed by the AI chip giant.
articles.body:
CoreWeave ( CRWV ) stock dropped 7% after trimming losses on Thursday as the fallout from Nvidia's leadership change rippled through the AI trade.

Nvidia ( NVDA ), which owns more than 10% of CoreWeave and is a major chip supplier to the AI infrastructure provider, is facing heightened scrutiny as the board announced Jensen Huang would resign immediately and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO .

CoreWeave stock has been volatile in recent weeks amid concerns about AI financing. Those fears appeared to ease on Wednesday after the company posted better-than-expected quarterly results and said it does not plan to take on more expensive debt through 2027.

Shares of other Nvidia partners have also come under pressure on Thursday.

Super Micro Computer ( SMCI ) stock plunged nearly 12% as Semafor reported widening scrutiny of Nvidia amid multiple US Justice Department investigations.

The report said one of the probes, on antitrust grounds, focuses on Nvidia, while the other two target AI infrastructure procurement firm Megaspeed and Super Micro. The California-based company makes AI servers which are stacked with Nvidia chips.

articles.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq turn higher as Nvidia stock slides after CEO Jensen Huang resigns
articles.summary: Stocks wobbled as tech investors assessed the fallout from reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's second affair and ouster.
articles.body: US stocks turned green late Thursday morning, paring earlier losses. Investors are weighing what the ousting of Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang means for the broader AI industry.The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) rose 0.3% while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) edged 0.1% higher. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) was up slightly, after getting a lift from Wednesday's chip stock-led rally. Nvidia stock tumbled 5% after trimming losses. The chipmaker has long stood at the heart of the AI investment boom that has powered this year's stock market. Nvidia's web of tie-ups with other AI companies also creates uncertainty about how great the fallout from Huang's affairs and potential dismissal could be for the market broadly.Follow the latest developments on Nvidia's CEO here.Some chipmakers, including Intel (INTC) and Micron (MU) fell, while others, such as Nvidia rival AMD (AMD) rose. The tumult, which is just the latest incident to raise investor doubts about the artificial intelligence trade, adds even more pressure for everything to go right in Anthropic's planned public debut next week. articles.title: Nvidia CFO solid pick for interim CEO, but company outlook is clouded, Wall Street says
articles.summary: Analysts on Wall Street have strong praise for Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress, but say the company's long-term outlook is still up in the air.
articles.body:
Wall Street analysts reacted with temporary relief on Thursday as Nvidia ( NVDA ) announced that CFO Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned following reports of alleged affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and an Nvidia executive.

Kress, who has served as Nvidia CFO, is seen as a steady hand amid the turmoil at the company.

Wall Street watchers say that, in the near future, Nvidia will be the revenue monster it's been since the start of the AI race, thanks to its existing product roadmap.

KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh wrote in a note to investors that Kress's appointment as interim CEO is constructive "given her tenure as CFO since 2013 and deep institutional knowledge of Nvidia's business and strategy."

But Huang, who led the company as a singular figure with dozens of direct reports, leaves a void that clouds Nvidia's long-term outlook.

As a result, several analysts lowered their price targets and ratings on the company's stock.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon, who reduced his price target from $400 to $200 and lowered his rating from Outperform to Market Perform, wrote in an investor note that Kress's appointment is a positive for the company.

"We aren't really worried about near-term impacts to the business as a result of the events of the past week, and of course the shares screen extremely cheap," he said.

But Rasgon raised concerns about a new CEO's ability to maneuver Nvidia's product pipeline, customer relationships, and more.

"We see considerable uncertainty around further newsflow that is probably going to be coming down the pipe, as well as the ability of any new CEO to truly fill Jensen's shoes given how tightly he managed the direction of the business and its relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, and the broader industry ecosystem," Rasgon wrote.

"Nothing would give us more pleasure than being able to revisit the story at some point, but we are having a hard time advocating stepping in here," Rasgon added.

Baird Equity Research analyst Tristan Gerra said Huang's resignation turns a page for Nvidia but that the episode hasn't hit its bottom yet.

"Headwinds include potential incremental senior management departures, H200 write-down charges, potential risk channel revenue adjustments, potential litigation [and] fines, uncertainties until [a] new CEO is announced along with the risk of some market share loss in 2029 as customers make contingency plans on a major top management transition and looking beyond the current product roadmap, along with more clarity on the next CEO's views regarding customer financings," Gerra wrote Thursday.
